summary: Records and record types from Cooper (2023) Appendix A11: distinguished labels and a boolean record well-formedness check (A11.1); record types as lists of plain or dependent fields, with dependent fields as shallow Coq functions (Val -> TTRType) plus a path list (A11.2); an inductive witnessing relation witnesses_rt over a TTRModel; a 'simple' merge (A11.3) that on shared labels keeps rt2's field rather than taking the meet; linguistic record types (man_runs, john_tall, dog_chases_cat) with chase(x,y) downgraded to a 0-ary ptype because multi-path dependencies are unsupported; one worked witnessing example (john_witnesses_ind_rt) and one trivial weakening theorem (rt_weaken_nil). The file's own summary block lists A9, A10, full recursive merge, A11.4 fixed points, A11.5-A11.8, relabelling and lambda-terms-as-labelled-sets as not covered, and six known issues including lists-not-sets and the universal Val domain vs Cooper's stratified universe.

sources.citation: Cooper, R. (2023). From Perception to Communication: A Theory of Types for Action and Meaning. Oxford University Press. Appendix A11 (records and record types).

definitions_mapped.source: A11.1: records are finite labelled sets with labels in L but not D, labels unique, every value witnessing some type
definitions_mapped.note: checks only the label conditions; the 'every value witnesses some type' clause is not enforced by is_record (witnessing lives separately in witnesses_rt); labelled sets are lists with no permutation-invariance lemma

definitions_mapped.coq: RecField (RF_plain / RF_dep with Val -> TTRType and list Path); RecType := list RecField
definitions_mapped.source: A11.2: record types as RT-flavoured labelled sets; dependent fields <l, <F, paths>>
definitions_mapped.note: dependent type families are shallow Coq functions inside the deep embedding (file's known issue 3); dependency restricted to a single path via hd with a dummy default (known issue 5)

definitions_mapped.source: A11.2 witnessing conditions: r : RT iff for each field r.l exists and witnesses T resp. F applied to the resolved dependency
definitions_mapped.note: clause-by-clause for plain fields; the dependent clause consults only the first declared path, so chase(x,y)-style multi-path dependencies are inexpressible

definitions_mapped.source: A11.3 merge: combine fields, taking the meet at shared labels
definitions_mapped.note: the comment states the meet clause but the code drops rt1's field on a label clash and keeps rt2's unchanged — no meet is computed; asymmetric and not the source operation

definitions_mapped.source: Cooper's situation-type worked examples ('a man runs' etc.)
definitions_mapped.note: dog_chases_cat renders chase as a 0-ary ptype (RF_plain) because two-path dependency is unsupported — flagged in a comment

definitions_mapped.source: width subtyping for record types (any record witnessing RT1 witnesses its sub-record-type RT2)
definitions_mapped.note: stated in prose; only the trivial nil instance rt_weaken_nil is proved

definitions_mapped.source: A9 modal systems; A10 stratified Type^n universes; full recursive merge with dependent fields; A11.4 fixed-point types; A11.5-A11.8; relabelling; lambda terms as labelled sets
definitions_mapped.note: acknowledged in the file's own NOT YET COVERED list

theorems.name: john_witnesses_ind_rt
theorems.source_claim: worked instance of A11.2 witnessing: the record {x = john} witnesses [x : Ind]
theorems.note: premise m_basic_assign M "Ind" (VStr "john") is a section Hypothesis discharged into the statement — an assumption, not an axiom; missed by anchored grep because it is section-indented (line 187)

theorems.name: rt_weaken_nil
theorems.source_claim: new (trivial nil instance of the width-subtyping rule stated only in a comment)
theorems.note: one-constructor proof (apply wrt_nil); the rubric's verifier would exclude it as trivial, leaving effectively one substantive theorem

evidence: The header and closing summary explicitly map the file to Cooper (2023) A11.1-A11.3 and list what is and is not covered, and the covered fragment does track the source's witnessing clauses field-by-field.
rt_merge_simple contradicts its own comment and the source: A11.3's meet at shared labels is replaced by keeping rt2's field (lines 124-131), a changed core definition.
Dependent fields support only one path (hd trick, line 99), so the file's own dog_chases_cat example cannot express chase(x,y) and substitutes a 0-ary ptype.
The headline structural claim in scope (width subtyping for record types) is stated only in prose; the sole general theorem proved is the trivial nil case, so headline claims of A11 are missing.
Zero Admitted, zero Axioms/Parameters; both Qed theorems close under a discharged section hypothesis only.
simplifications: single-path dependencies instead of Cooper's n-tuples of paths
record well-formedness checks labels only, deferring value-typing to witnesses_rt
labelled sets as lists (order artifact, no permutation lemma)
Val as a universal domain instead of Cooper's stratified Type^n universes
omissions: A11.5-A11.8 (unique identifiers, dependency/generalization, restriction T||r, path alignment)
additions: is_distinguished hard-codes the reserved-label inventory as a boolean predicate

determination_rationale: Provisional, evidenced only by this thin pilot: the covered core already required re-founding moves — dependent record types become a hybrid shallow/deep encoding (Coq functions over a universal Val domain, collapsing Cooper's stratified Type^n universes), multi-path dependency is cut to one path, and merge is replaced by an operation that is not the source's (rt2-wins instead of meet). No headline A11 claim (subtyping, merge laws, fixed points) is proved. Nothing here diagnoses a foundational impossibility ('cannot'), but nothing supports as-is or slight-modification either: what exists is a partial formalization with changed/simplified core definitions, which is the rubric's criterion for determination 3. A deeper treatment of A10 stratification and A11.4 fixed points could revise this either way.

artifact_classes.description: Val as an unstratified universal domain in place of Cooper's Type^n hierarchy, with shallow Val -> TTRType functions inside the deep embedding (the file's known issues 2-3) — type/value structure collapsed

missing native structure: no dependent record types with labels/paths in the substrate, so labelled sets are lists (ordering artifact, known issue 1) and multi-path dependency is faked by hd on a path list (known issue 5)
no decidability results (known issue 6); witnessing is propositional rather than computational (known issue 4), so record/type checking does not compute

notes: Record produced by the batch audit sweep of 2026-09-05; the file predates the atlas zero-axiom discipline but happens to declare no Axioms/Parameters (its one Hypothesis is section-discharged) — its weakness is coverage (2 theorems, 1 trivial), not assumptions; the anchored theorem grep undercounts (1) because john_witnesses_ind_rt is section-indented.
